statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail risk is low at 13% while stress is elevated at 53%. NQ futures have extended their overnight recovery to about 29,468 against a 29,300.50 prior close but sit roughly 50 points below the session high, so retracement is still occurring inside a band of about 0.6% after a fourth consecutive lower Nasdaq-100 close.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD across the full 24-hour horizon. Conditional risk is concentrated in two checkpoints: the 13:00-14:00 UTC hour, published as the narrow danger window, which contains the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMI; and the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour, in which August monthly options expiration settles into the cash close ahead of the 21:00 UTC weekend halt. Both map to EA_ON rather than to a block. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures extend an orderly overnight recovery with retracements still available, leaving mean reversion intact into a flash PMI, the cash open and August monthly expiration
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,213.17 on 20 August, down 0.72% and a fourth consecutive lower close, with the index tracking roughly 2% lower on the week. That session was driven by the bond market rather than by earnings: the 10Y closed at 4.69% and the 30Y at 5.24%, each about 4bp higher, after the relief from the Treasury's enlarged buyback announcement proved short-lived. Overnight, NQ futures have recovered to roughly 29,467.75 against a 29,300.50 prior close, trading a 29,341.50 to 29,518.50 band and currently sitting about 50 points below the high of that band. The path is a drift higher with higher lows, but price is not holding the session extreme and pullbacks are still forming, which is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that defines tail risk for a mean-reversion approach. Cross-asset evidence is mixed rather than aligned. VIX is 15.66, down 2.19% from a 16.01 close, and the 2Y is unchanged at 4.20%, both consistent with orderly conditions. Against that, the 10Y is 3bp firmer at 4.71% and the 30Y is 5.25%, still close to its highest level since 2007, so the week's central pressure has not been resolved. WTI at $86.48 and Brent at $93.33 are marginally lower on the day but track a second consecutive weekly gain of about 5%, with Strait of Hormuz flows still constrained and a US Treasury announcement on Iran sanctions scheduled for Monday. Gold is firmer by more than 1.5%, indicating a live hedging bid rather than a broad risk-off flush. Delayed latest-session context shows all eight tracked megacaps and all seven tracked semiconductors higher with mean gains of about 0.59% and 0.70%; that is confirmation of tone only and is not treated as evidence of the current price path. The scheduled stack for the day is the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMI, the 17:00 UTC Baker Hughes rig count, August monthly options expiration settling into the 20:00 UTC cash close and the 21:00 UTC weekend halt. None of these is an observed one-way structure, so they raise conditional stress and shape the danger window rather than lifting current tail toward the block threshold.

lookbackSummary: Twenty of the 24 preceding clock-hours have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable with null assessment fields; no past opinion is reconstructed from later information. The four available slots are 2026-08-21T01:00:00Z with tail 12%, stress 59%, confidence 83% and a mixed dominant mode; 06:00:00Z with tail 12%, stress 57%, confidence 84% and mixed; 07:00:00Z with tail 12%, stress 55%, confidence 85% and mixed; and 08:00:00Z with tail 12%, stress 54%, confidence 86% and mixed. Tail was stable at 12% across all four, while stress stepped steadily lower as the overnight recovery held and volatility decayed, and confidence rose as the evidence base filled out. The current assessment lifts tail one point to 13% because the overnight band has extended upward to a higher high and a higher low, and lowers stress one point to 53% because VIX has decayed further and the front end of the curve is unchanged. The unavailable hours cover the 20 August US session and the Asian session that followed it; both are described in the body from current sources rather than back-filled as past model opinions.
outlookSummary: The horizon runs from late European morning through the full US session and then ends inside the weekend futures halt. Early hours are scored at low tail risk on the contained, two-sided overnight band. Conditional risk peaks in the 13:00-14:00 UTC hour, which contains both the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMI, and is published as the narrow danger window. A second, slightly lower peak falls on the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour, where August monthly options expiration settles into the cash close alongside pre-weekend risk reduction. From 21:00 UTC the CME halt removes the continuous price path entirely, so tail falls to a structural floor near 9-10% for the remaining thirteen hours and confidence decays gradually with the age of the last observed price path. Every hour of the horizon maps to EA_ON because no published tail score reaches the 25% block threshold. Beyond the horizon, the named next-week checkpoints are a Treasury press conference on Iran sanctions on Monday, the Q2 GDP second estimate and July core PCE on 26 August, NVIDIA results after the US close the same day, and the Jackson Hole symposium from 27 to 29 August.
